audit_findings.title: Redeemable noncontrolling interests are absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.561416 billion filed at 2026-06-30, equal to 10.7% of the $14.531 billion base equity value and $22.92 per modeled share before offsetting acquired earnings; net effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The put settlement is a claim on the common-equity bridge, while exercising the puts would transfer the associated minority owner earnings into future OE.
audit_findings.evidence: If these put provisions were exercised, the Company would be required to purchase the third-party owners’ equity interests, generally at the appraised fair market value of the equity interests or in certain cases at a predetermined multiple of earnings or cash flows attributable to the equity interests put to the Company, intended to approximate fair value.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge omission is demonstrated and large enough to change the valuation conclusion if treated as an unoffset claim. However, deducting the entire balance without adding the earnings acquired through settlement would also be incorrect. The filed record does not isolate those earnings or the timing and probability of exercise, so the net direction is mixed and the net amount remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each put's exercise window, current settlement estimate and attributable minority earnings; rerun all scenarios using a probability-weighted settlement outflow and corresponding transition of earnings to DaVita.

audit_findings.title: Parent earnings may be combined with consolidated cash-flow add-backs
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 NCI income was $331.913 million and NCI distributions were $324.270 million, respectively 33.7% and 32.9% of the $985.2 million OE anchor; the actual OE error is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The OE numerator starts with income attributable to DaVita but applies consolidated depreciation, capital expenditure and working-capital adjustments, potentially assigning subsidiary cash flows belonging to minority owners to the parent shares.
audit_findings.evidence: Noncontrolling interests represent third-party equity interests in entities which are consolidated by the Company for financial statement reporting purposes.
audit_findings.explanation: Given the supplied construction, the perimeter inconsistency is a demonstrated methodological error, not merely a possible future risk. Subtracting distributions does not establish parent ownership of the remaining consolidated add-backs because distributions can differ from current-period attributable cash generation. The exposed amounts are large enough to change value, although the correction could increase or decrease OE depending on minority depreciation, maintenance capex, working capital and retained cash.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild every historical OE observation on one consistent perimeter: either consolidated OE followed by an explicit NCI claim deduction, or parent-attributable OE using proportionate D&A, maintenance capex and working-capital movements; then refit the anchor and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The latest balance-sheet financing may not match the historical interest burden
audit_findings.magnitude: Debt principal increased $502.933 million between 2025-12-31 and 2026-06-30; first-half 2026 debt expense was $295.387 million, $14.270 million above first-half 2025, and its simple $590.774 million annualization is $10.848 million or 1.1% of anchor OE above FY2025 debt expense
audit_findings.mechanism: Because this is an equity-level OE model, interest expense enters OE directly; using June 2026 cash and financing while anchoring OE through FY2025 may omit the full recurring interest cost of the later debt.
audit_findings.evidence: Debt expense increased primarily due to an increase in our long-term debt balance related to the third quarter 2024 issuance of 6.875% senior notes due 2032 and the second quarter 2025 issuance of 6.75% senior notes due 2033, as well as the expiration of our 2019 interest rate cap agreements on June 30, 2024, which had lower rates than our currently effective interest rate caps.
audit_findings.explanation: The date mismatch is demonstrated, but the record does not establish the normalized annual after-tax interest burden. The June borrowing occurred late in the first half, while rates, hedges and debt deployment also changed. The observed run-rate difference is modest relative to anchor OE, but incomplete seasoning of the new debt prevents a supported conclusion that the full valuation effect is immaterial.
audit_findings.action: Calculate pro forma annual interest expense at the 2026-06-30 principal balances, contractual margins, fixed-note coupons, hedge strikes and unused-facility costs; apply the parent tax rate, replace the historical interest burden in normalized OE and rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: Prior-period IKC revenue may distort the 2025 OE observation
audit_findings.magnitude: $171.385 million of 2025 IKC revenue related to prior-year performance obligations, equal to 14.7% of 2025 OE and 17.4% of anchor OE; the related OE and cash-flow effect is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Delayed IKC recognition can misallocate earnings, receivables and operating cash flow among historical OE observations and thereby alter both the latest observation and the fitted OE trend.
audit_findings.evidence: For its IKC business, the Company recognized revenues for performance obligations satisfied in previous years of $ 171,385 , $ 116,336 , and $ 94,361 during the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The delayed recognition is demonstrated, but the supplied amount is revenue rather than incremental OE. The record does not show the associated medical-cost development, operating expenses, taxes, receivable movements or cash collections. Because similar prior-period revenue was recognized in 2023 and 2024, normalization may redistribute rather than remove value, leaving both direction and materiality unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $171.385 million and the corresponding $94.361 million and $116.336 million prior-year amounts through IKC operating profit, claims estimates, contract assets, receivables and cash collections; restate OE by performance year, refit the trend and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Unaccrued legal and regulatory claims are not represented in the bridge
audit_findings.mechanism: Unrecorded settlements, penalties and defense costs would reduce the equity bridge or future OE, while mandated changes to referral, joint-venture, billing or insurance practices could reduce recurring OE and growth.
audit_findings.evidence: Additionally, in some cases, no estimate of the possible loss or range of loss in excess of amounts accrued, if any, can be made because of the inherently unpredictable nature of legal proceedings and regulatory matters, which also may be impacted by various factors, including, without limitation, that they may involve indeterminate claims for monetary damages or may involve fines, penalties or non-monetary remedies; present novel legal theories or legal uncertainties; involve disputed facts; represent a shift in regulatory policy; are in the early stages of the proceedings; or may result in a change of business practices.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved exposure rather than a demonstrated valuation error: filed accruals were individually immaterial, but the company could not estimate some losses above accruals. Existing False Claims Act, insurance, antitrust and regulatory matters make the exposure present rather than merely forward-looking, yet the record supplies neither probabilities nor loss ranges sufficient to establish materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain proceeding-specific status, claimed damages, comparable settlements, defense-cost estimates, insurance recoveries and counsel probability assessments; model probability-weighted one-time cash claims in the bridge and recurring practice-change effects in OE and growth.

audit_findings.title: The stated dilution ceiling may not use maximum PSU issuance
audit_findings.magnitude: At most 0.766 million filed maximum PSU shares for this isolated issue, equal to 1.12% of the 68.119 million modeled share count; assuming all are additionally omitted lowers base value from $213.32 to $210.95 and buy-below from $149.32 to $147.66
audit_findings.mechanism: Any omitted maximum PSU issuance increases the fully diluted denominator and reduces value per share without changing enterprise or equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: Includes 766 shares of common stock reserved for issuance in connection with performance share units at the maximum number of shares issuable thereunder.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the ceiling already contains maximum PSU issuance remains unresolved, but the filed maximum provides a conservative scale test. Even treating all 0.766 million shares as incremental reduces base value by only $2.37 per share and leaves the $183.99 market price $36.33 above the recalculated buy-below price. The isolated finding therefore cannot change the stated purchase conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the 2.995 million outstanding stock units, 3.723 million plan-table amount, maximum PSU factor, SSAR settlement shares and subsequent grants to eliminate double counting; rerun per-share values only if the total omitted dilution exceeds this isolated 0.766 million-share bound.
